questions.stem: Which statement best describes Addressing space in Cilium?

options.text: Concept that is specific to Cilium and is not related to `Kubernetes' EndpointSlice`_.

Cilium will assign IPs to pods out of the PodCIDR assigned to the specific Kubernetes node. By using `Alias IP ranges <https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/alias-ip>`_, these IPs are natively routable on Google Cloud's network without additional encapsulation or route distribution.

When running together with an orchestration system such as Kubernetes, the list of all nodes in the cluster including their associated allocation prefix node is made available to each agent automatically. New nodes joining the cluster will automatically be incorporated into the mesh.

Due to not depending on any underlying networking limitations, the available addressing space is potentially much larger and allows to run any number of pods per node if the PodCIDR size is configured accordingly.

questions.explanation: Due to not depending on any underlying networking limitations, the available addressing space is potentially much larger and allows to run any number of pods per node if the PodCIDR size is configured accordingly.

optionRationale.c: This describes Auto-configuration, not Addressing space.

optionRationale.b: This describes Addressing, not Addressing space.

questions.stem: An engineer executes the command `kubectl exec "$FORTIO_POD" -c fortio -- /usr/bin/fortio load -c 2 -qps 0 -n 20 http://echo-service:8080`. Based on the provided output, what is the distribution of HTTP response codes received?

options.text: 19 requests returned code 200 and 1 request returned code 503.
20 requests returned code 200 and 0 requests returned code 503.
10 requests returned code 200 and 10 requests returned code 503.
18 requests returned code 200 and 2 requests returned code 503.

questions.explanation: The output for the command with `-c 2` explicitly states `Code 200 : 19 (95.0 %)` and `Code 503 : 1 (5.0 %)`. This indicates that out of the 20 total calls, 19 were successful and 1 triggered the circuit breaker with a 503 error.

optionRationale.b: Incorrect. The output clearly shows one instance of `Code 503 : 1 (5.0 %)`, so not all requests were successful.
optionRationale.c: Incorrect. The output shows 19 successful requests, not 10. The 50% split is not supported by the data.
optionRationale.d: Incorrect. The output shows only one 503 error, not two. The count for code 200 is 19, not 18.

questions.stem: In the scenario where the engineer increases the concurrent connections to 4 using the flag `-c 4`, the output shows multiple `Non ok http code` warnings. What specific HTTP status code is associated with these warnings in the log entries?
questions.explanation: The log entries for the run with `-c 4` contain multiple lines such as `{"ts":1692767495.822424,"level":"warn","file":"http_client.go","line":1104,"msg":"Non ok http code","code":"503","status":"HTTP/1.1 503","thread":"3","run":"0"}`. The `code` field is consistently "503".

questions.stem: An engineer is testing the L7 circuit breaker and observes that with 2 concurrent connections, only 1 out of 20 requests fails with a 503 error. When the engineer increases the concurrency to 4 connections, the output shows multiple 503 errors. According to the excerpt, what does the presence of the 503 response code indicate?

options.text: It indicates that the circuit breaker has been triggered.
It indicates that the Fortio client has crashed.
It indicates that the echo-service is completely down.
It indicates that the Kubernetes pod is restarting.

questions.explanation: The excerpt explicitly states: "From the above output, you can see that the response code of some requests is 503, which triggers a circuit breaker." Therefore, the 503 code is the indicator that the circuit breaker mechanism has activated.

optionRationale.b: Incorrect. The Fortio client continues to run and report statistics; it does not crash.
optionRationale.c: Incorrect. The service is not completely down, as some requests (or in the first test, most) still return 200, and the 503 is specifically linked to the circuit breaker, not total unavailability.
optionRationale.d: Incorrect. There is no mention of pod restarts in the output or explanation.

questions.stem: An engineer applies a `CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy` to deny all traffic by default. When an external client sends a request to the `/details` endpoint, the response is a 403 Forbidden. According to the Hubble flow logs provided, what is the status of the HTTP request flow?

options.text: DROPPED
FORWARDED
ALLOWED
DENIED

questions.explanation: The Hubble output explicitly shows the line `http-request DROPPED (HTTP/1.1 GET http://172.19.255.194/details/1)`. Although the client receives a 403 response, the flow status for the request itself is recorded as DROPPED.

optionRationale.b: FORWARDED is the status of the http-response, not the http-request.
optionRationale.c: ALLOWED is not the specific status shown in the log for the dropped request.
optionRationale.d: DENIED is a general concept but the specific log status is DROPPED.

questions.stem: After applying a default deny policy, an engineer observes that the HTTP response to a denied request is forwarded with a 403 status. Which identity is associated with the source of the denied request in the Hubble logs?

options.text: world
cluster
reserved:ingress
default

questions.explanation: The Hubble log entry for the dropped request shows the source identity as `(world)`: `172.19.0.1:34104 (ingress) -> default/cilium-ingress-basic-ingress:80 (world)`. This indicates the traffic originated from outside the cluster.

optionRationale.b: cluster is mentioned later as a target identity for allowed traffic, not the source of the denied external traffic.
optionRationale.c: reserved:ingress is the identity of the ingress gateway itself, not the external client.
optionRationale.d: default is the namespace, not the identity of the external source.

questions.stem: An engineer runs `kubectl get gateway -A` and observes that the `PROGRAMMED` column is empty for a Gateway named `http-gateway`. The `CLASS` is `cilium` and an `ADDRESS` is present. According to the provided documentation, what is the most likely cause and the recommended action?

options.text: The Gateway API CRDs are not installed; the engineer should install the CRDs.
Gateway API is not enabled in the Cilium configuration; the engineer should ensure it is enabled.
The LoadBalancer implementation is missing; the engineer should install a LoadBalancer service.
The Gateway class is incorrect; the engineer should change the class to `envoy`.

questions.explanation: The excerpt states: 'If the `Programmed true` indicator is missing, make sure that Gateway API is enabled in the Cilium configuration.' Since the address is present, the LoadBalancer is likely fine, and the class is correct, the missing programmed status points to the configuration setting.

optionRationale.a: The excerpt states that if the resource type is not found, CRDs should be checked, but a missing 'Programmed' indicator specifically points to the Cilium configuration.
optionRationale.c: The excerpt states that if no IP appears (address missing), a LoadBalancer implementation might be missing. Here, an address is present.
optionRationale.d: The excerpt states Cilium only programs Gateways with the class `cilium`. The class is already `cilium`, so this is not the issue.

citations.title: Checking resources
citations.quote: If the ``Programmed true`` indicator is missing, make sure that Gateway API is enabled in the Cilium configuration.

questions.stem: Which header does Envoy set to the trusted client address, based on the X-Forwarded-For header, regardless of what that address turns out to be?

options.text: X-Forwarded-For
X-Envoy-External-Address
X-Real-IP
X-Client-IP

questions.explanation: The excerpt states that Envoy will also set the X-Envoy-External-Address header to the trusted client address, whatever that turns out to be, based on X-Forwarded-For.

optionRationale.a: X-Forwarded-For is the header that is appended to or read from, not the one set to the trusted client address by Envoy in this specific context.
optionRationale.c: X-Real-IP is not mentioned in the excerpt.
optionRationale.d: X-Client-IP is not mentioned in the excerpt.

citations.title: Source IP Visibility
citations.quote: Envoy will also set the ``X-Envoy-External-Address`` header to the trusted client address, whatever that turns out to be, based on ``X-Forwarded-For``.
